Messages.Author: XZealot
Messages.Body:
In an effort to eliminate the politicking going on at the tables, what
do you think of a Team Format with two teams of three players
competing at a six person table with the teams set up before hand?

I know that six player games take a long time, but I think that teams
organizing themselves beforehand would create synergisms between their
decks. This would actually shorten the game. What you do think?

Comment Welcome,
Norman S. Brown, Jr
XZealot
Archon of the Swamp

I like it.

A perhaps novel twist (to keep the game from degenerating too badly after the
first oust): allow only 3 VPs at the six-player table.

When your prey is ousted or withdraws, 1 VP is awarded, and both you and your
prey are eliminated. The 1 VP goes to your team if your prey was ousted; it goes
to your prey's team if your prey withdraws. In the case of ousting, the six pool
reward (or whatever amount) is divided among the remaining team members as they
see fit.

Oh, and "no table talk", since there are only two sides. :-)

If four teams are interested at the NAC or the EC or Dragon*Con or Gen*Con, I'll
be happy to officiate an unsanctioned tournament in this format for them.

No. I mean limited VPs by removing the predator of a Methuselah who is ousted.

>> When your prey is ousted or withdraws, 1 VP is awarded, and both you and your
>> prey are eliminated. The 1 VP goes to your team if your prey was ousted; it goes
>> to your prey's team if your prey withdraws. In the case of ousting, the six pool
>> reward (or whatever amount) is divided among the remaining team members as they
>> see fit.
>
> Interesting.
>
>> Oh, and "no table talk", since there are only two sides. :-)

... except for slitting the VP pool reward, of course.

One more thing: simultaneous ousting.

If simultaneous ousting would result in an uneven number of players ousted (more
from one team than another, after applying the above rule), then don't apply the
above rule beyond what is needed to make parity.

This will result in more than 3 VPs being awarded in the game.

Examples (A-F seated around the table in that order).

If C and D are ousted, then the rule would have B C and D removed. In this case,
only C and D are removed. Each team gets 1 VP. (The six pool for C goes to B as
usual).

If C D and E are ousted, then B-E are removed as usual. Since B was removed
without being ousted, his remaining teammate (F) gets the six pool reward. The
ACE team gets 1 VP (for D). The BDF team gets 2 VPs (for C and E).

If C D and F are ousted, then C-F are removed (B is not removed). E's 6-pool
reward goes to A. The ACE team gets 2 VPs (for D and F). The BDF team gets 1 VP.

If C-F are ousted, then B stays and gets 6 pool. Each team gets 2 VPs.

If B-F are ousted, A's team wins (4 to 2).

If A-F are ousted, it's a draw. (3 to 3).

@n2g2000hse.googlegroups.com:

Nice. Team play 6-player should be shorter than standard 5-player,
anyways. You only need to have three ousts occur, for the win, and once
you have a one-man advantage, tables can theoretically accelerate
quickly.

Emperor-style Magic co-opted and modified the predator-prey relationship
from VTES... It might be interesting to playtest or thought-test a few
different kinds of table layouts, and see what is most interesting;

Team A, players 1,2,3
Team B, players 1,2,3

Alternating Seating A1-> B1 -> A2 -> B2 -> A3 -> B3 (standard pred-prey
applies, until the table collapses by a player... then what?)

Emperor Seating A2 -> A1* -> A3 -> B2 -> B1* -> B3 (Players A2,A3,B2,B3
have standard pred-prey relationship. A1*, B1* "Emperors" can "reach" up
to two seat positions in either table direction with D effects)

Others?

Alternate seating is the most strightforward. Some deck mods caan be
made for the team dynamic, but it will play out much like what we expect
from VTES.

Emperor Seating could have some potential to see some _really_ different
decks, particularly from the emperor seat. COuld be neat to see.

Messages.Author: LSJ
Messages.Body:



In MtG Emperor format, the reach was uniformly 2, even for the Generals (the
non-Emperor players).

Besides that, if you wanted to restrict reach to 1 for the generals, your "prey"
would be "adjacent player of the opposite team" rather than the standard
pred-prey (no sense having A2's prey be her team's Emperor, I think).

A3's prey is B2. B2's prey is A3.
A3's predator is B2. B2's predator is 3.

The Emperor has no prey and no predator until one of his teammates is ousted.

For more:
http://www.wizards.com/default.asp?x=magic/rules/emperor

Messages.Author: Frederick Scott
Messages.Body:
"LSJ" <vte...@white-wolf.com> wrote in message
news:iyugi.27151$YL5....@newssvr29.news.prodigy.net...

> Not if it is forbidden. The "no table talk" sentence above is introducing a rule; it is not merely an observation of the

Bleh. Sounds too anal to me. Why not just let people talk, albeit (as in
the normal game) no showing anyone cards outside of where game mechanics
allow for it and all talk must be audible to all players? The team concept
is novel enough without throwing in a "no talking" rule. The charms of
unforced errors based on team members' lack of ability to communicate verbally
sounds cutesy but cutesyness isn't really that entertaining in the long run
compared the ability to just play out the tactics in a more or less "normal"
(i.e. talking-allowed) environment. I think people would ultimately appreciate
the latter more. And it also prevents snarkiness around the edges of the no-
talking rule which people would attempt to evade in spirit by making faces,
grunting, screaming, urinating on themselves**, etc. when they wished to
communicate something to their teammates.

Fred

** - Hopefully only on themselves... :-P
